This aquamarine was one of my first faceted gemstones. I originally purchased this Stone from Nature's Treasures in Austin Texas as a mineral specimen and ended up cutting it. It has some icicle-like inclusions that add a frosty touch to this stone's pale color.

Aquamarine is a blue to blue-green variety of the mineral beryl (the same mineral family as emerald). The blue color comes from iron impurities in the crystal structure. The name literally means "sea water" in Latin.

This stone was mined in Ouro Preto, Brazil and purchased rough from a private seller in Bastrop, Texas. This barion style square cut, called "Square Radiant Topaz" was designed by A. Collins. Imperial Topaz is the most prized variety of topaz. The name reportedly comes from 19th-century Russia, where the finest specimens were reserved for the Czar's royal family. Imperial topaz is much rarer than the common blue or white topaz seen in most jewelry stores. Unlike most blue topaz (which is irradiated), imperial topaz gets its color naturally from chromium impurities.

This topaz comes from the Tepetate deposit, located in the Villa de Arriaga Municipality of San Luis Potosí, discovered in the 1960s. The name "Tepetate" is derived from the native Nahuatl word 'Tepetlatl', referring to hardened volcanic, rhyolitic topaz-bearing tuffs. The deposit from which this stone was taken is largely historic (1960-1990), and the material is now scarce.

Kryptonite Nanosital in a Superman cut is sure to dazzle with sparkling opalescent colors. Nanosital is a remarkable lab-created material that faithfully replicates the optical properties and vibrant colors of natural gemstones at a fraction of the cost. Its consistent clarity and lack of inclusions mean you get eye-clean stones every time, without the ethical concerns or environmental impact associated with mining. The material is durable enough for everyday jewelry while offering colors—from rich emerald greens to deep sapphire blues—that remain stable and won't fade over time. For anyone who loves the beauty of gemstones but wants an affordable, sustainable, and reliably gorgeous option, nanosital delivers on all fronts.
